data.text: The Majuli VR tour aims to digitally preserve the ecological and cultural heritage of the disappearing island. The evaluation study measures usability factors such as engagement, presence, comfort, and cybersickness. Data is collected through controlled experiments and structured questionnaires using subjective, objective, or behavioral measures.
points: The Majuli VR tour aims to digitally preserve the ecological and cultural heritage of the disappearing island.
The evaluation study measures usability factors such as engagement, presence, comfort, and cybersickness.
Data is collected through controlled experiments and structured questionnaires using subjective, objective, or behavioral measures.

data.text: The study involved 27 volunteers divided into categories of pilgrims, students, and tourists. Most participants were aged between 23 and 40 and had prior VR experience, while all were familiar with joystick-based controllers and had normal or corrected-to-normal vision. The setup used a Meta Quest 2 HMD connected to a PC with a GeForce GTX 1080 GPU, with participants seated on swivel chairs during the evaluation.
points: The study involved 27 volunteers divided into three categories: pilgrims, students, and tourists.
Participants were aged between 23 and 40, and most had prior VR experience.
All participants had normal or corrected-to-normal vision and were familiar with joystick-based controllers.
The evaluation used a Meta Quest 2 HMD connected to a PC with a GeForce GTX 1080 GPU.
Participants were seated on swivel chairs while performing the tasks.

data.text: Presence is a psychological state measured by the QEP questionnaire, which uses a 1 to 7 Likert scale and includes 19 core and 3 optional items. For the Majuli VR tour, the QEP questionnaire was tailored with two subjective items. Cybersickness is measured using the simulator sickness questionnaire (SSQ) with a 0 to 3 scale. These scores are compared before and after exposure to evaluate the VR tour assessment design.
points: Presence is a psychological state measured by the QEP questionnaire.
The QEP questionnaire uses a 1 to 7 Likert scale and includes 19 core items and 3 optional items.
The QEP questionnaire was tailored with two subjective items for the Majuli VR tour.
Cybersickness is measured using the simulator sickness questionnaire (SSQ).
The SSQ uses a 0 to 3 scale to measure and compare symptoms before and after exposure.

data.text: Pre-experiment training can reduce familiarity or prior-experience bias. Evaluations use questionnaires to measure cybersickness and presence, with exploration lasting 45 to 50 minutes to provide sufficient time for exploration while minimizing the possibility of cybersickness. Controlled experiments require defining users, preparing setups, and establishing procedures that eliminate biases.

data.text: The virtual tour of Majuli Island achieved a "good presence," meaning users felt reasonably well located while exploring the environment. Participants who had previously visited the island provided more favorable opinions across all factors despite having higher expectations. Furthermore, prior exposure to digital or virtual tours helps users gain a better experience.
points: Presence was measured using involvement, interface quality, adaptation or immersion, and visual fidelity.
The virtual tour achieved a "good presence" rating, meaning users felt reasonably well located while exploring.
Previous visitors gave more favorable opinions for all factors despite having higher expectations.
Prior exposure to digital or virtual tours helps users gain a better experience.

data.text: The cyber sickness evaluation of the Majuli virtual tour used the SSQ questionnaire to collect pre- and post-exposure data. While box plots showed little difference for nausea and disorientation, a Wilcoxon signed-rank test revealed statistically significant differences for oculomotor and total sickness items. This significant change in total sickness indicates that the Majuli virtual tour design had some effect on total sickness.
points: The SSQ questionnaire was used to collect pre- and post-exposure data for cyber sickness.
Box plots showed little difference in nausea and disorientation, but some difference in total and oculomotor severity.
A Wilcoxon signed-rank test revealed statistically significant differences in oculomotor and total sickness items.
The statistically significant change in total sickness indicates that the Majuli virtual tour design had some effect on total sickness.

data.text: Presence measures for the Majuli VR Tour were mostly good, and prior experience may lead to even better results. Certain cybersickness items were not found to affect severity, but the oculomotor component may be affected, which may lead to some effect on total sickness.
points: Presence measures for the Majuli VR Tour were mostly good, and prior experience may lead to even better results.
Certain cybersickness items may not affect severity, but the oculomotor component may affect total sickness.
